shodasavarga (16).arithmetic_note: The four explicit values plus half for each of the remaining twelve sum to 18.5, not the 20 the scheme is named for. Either the scan has lost the hora and drekkana assignments of sloka 124's first pada, or this recension's shodasavarga vishvas genuinely do not close. The discrepancy is PUBLISHED, not patched.

procedure: choose a scheme: shadvarga (6 vargas), saptavarga (7), dasavarga (10) or shodasavarga (16)
for each varga in the scheme, find the graha's dignity relative to that varga's lord
score 20 / 20 / 15 / 10 / 7 / 5 vishvas for exalted-or-own / great friend / friend / neutral / enemy / great enemy
multiply that score by the varga's own weight from the scheme table, and divide by 20
sum over the vargas of the scheme; the total is out of 20

grading.below 5: no result at all (फलदो न हि)

conclusion.adhimitra_ambiguity: Sloka 126's second half is printed 'पूर्णं विश्वाबलं विंशतिः स्यादधिमित्रके'. It can be read either as (a) full strength is twenty, and likewise in the great-friend's place, or (b) full strength [in one's own or exaltation] is twenty, and in the great friend's place [eighteen]. The modern handbooks read 18 for adhimitra. This scan does not settle it and the ambiguity is recorded rather than resolved.

conclusion.sanskrit: वर्गभेदानहं वक्ष्ये मैत्रेय त्वं विधारय ॥ षड्वर्गाः सप्तवर्गाश्च दशवर्गो षोडशवर्गकाः ॥ ९१ ॥ भवंति वर्गसंयोगे षड्वर्गे किंशुकादयः ॥ द्वाभ्यां किंशुकनामा च त्रिभिर्व्यंजनमुच्यते ॥ ९२ ॥ ...
conclusion.engine_rendering: I shall declare the divisions of the vargas. There are the six-varga, seven-varga, ten-varga and sixteen-varga schemes. In the six-varga scheme the names beginning with kimshuka arise on combination: by two it is called kimshuka, by three vyanjana, by four chamara, by five chhatra, by six kundala and by seven mukuta.
conclusion.dignity_counted: स्वोच्चमूलत्रिकोणस्वभवनाधिपति - own exaltation, moolatrikona, own house and lordship, counted from the graha's own arudha's kendra lords (sloka 101)
conclusion.disqualifiers: अस्तंगता ग्रहजिता नीचगा दुर्बलास्तथा - combust, defeated in war, debilitated or weak grahas produce a yoga-destroying result instead (sloka 102)
conclusion.refused: The tier NAME is a defensible thing to report once the vargas are computed. The emperor/kingship predicate attached to the higher tiers is NOT, and is refused - this is the same refusal already recorded for adhyaya 28's raja-yoga ladder in bphs_rule_manifest.json.
conclusion.output_policy: refused_for_the_kingship_predicate; the tier name alone is renderable_with_source

conclusion.engine_rendering: Eight of the sixteen vargas have their computation rule encoded from this chapter (D1, D2, D3, D4, D7, D10, D12, D30, D60 - nine counting D60; D9 is already implemented in the engine and encoded elsewhere). Six do not.
conclusion.why: Their defining slokas fall in the stretch of adhyaya 3 between slokas 66 and 76 and between 79 and 87, which was not read verse-by-verse in this pass. They are NOT blocked - the pages are legible in the same scan; they are simply unmined, and saying so is the honest status.
conclusion.consequence: The dasavarga and shodasavarga vimsopaka schemes cannot be completed until those six are read. The shadvarga and saptavarga schemes can, because they need only D1, D2, D3, D7, D9, D12 and D30, all of which are now encoded.
